## Solution

**Yes**, the rank of $M$ is at most $n-1$.

**Key observation.** For a permutation $P$, order the indices by increasing priority: $i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_n$ so that $p_{i_1} < p_{i_2} < \cdots < p_{i_n}$. Define the partial sums
$$A_k := 1 + \sum_{m=1}^{k} x_{i_m}, \qquad k = 0, 1, \ldots, n,$$
so $A_0 = 1$ and $A_n = 1 + \sum_{j=1}^n x_j$.

For index $i_k$, the set $\{j : p_j < p_{i_k}\}$ is exactly $\{i_1, \ldots, i_{k-1}\}$, hence
$$\sum_{p_j < p_{i_k}} x_j = \sum_{m=1}^{k-1} x_{i_m} = A_{k-1} - 1.$$

Therefore
$$y_{i_k} = \log\!\left(1 + \frac{x_{i_k}}{A_{k-1}}\right) = \log\!\left(\frac{A_{k-1} + x_{i_k}}{A_{k-1}}\right) = \log\!\left(\frac{A_k}{A_{k-1}}\right) = \log A_k - \log A_{k-1}.$$

**Telescoping.** Summing over all indices:
$$\sum_{i=1}^n y_i = \sum_{k=1}^n \bigl(\log A_k - \log A_{k-1}\bigr) = \log A_n - \log A_0 = \log\!\left(1 + \sum_{j=1}^n x_j\right).$$

The right-hand side depends **only on $X$**, not on the permutation $P$. Hence for every permutation $P$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^n (Y_P)_i = \log\!\left(1 + \sum_{j=1}^n x_j\right) =: C.$$

**Conclusion.** Every row of $M$ is of the form $Y_P - Y_{P_1}$, and
$$\sum_{i=1}^n \bigl((Y_P)_i - (Y_{P_1})_i\bigr) = C - C = 0.$$

Thus every row of $M$ lies in the $(n-1)$-dimensional subspace $H = \{v \in \mathbb{R}^n : \mathbf{1}^\top v = 0\}$. Consequently,
$$\operatorname{rank}(M) \le \dim H = n - 1.$$

All output vectors $Y_P$ lie on the affine hyperplane $\{y : \mathbf{1}^\top y = C\}$ of dimension $n-1$. $\blacksquare$
